The permission-request handler resolves allow/deny decisions and builds event input, defining a sensitive approval boundary.
Post-tool-use request/outcome types serialize completed tool context and convert handler outputs, defining the after-execution event contract.
Pre-tool-use request/outcome handling lets handlers inspect or update tool input before execution and encodes serialization failure behavior.
Session-end request/outcome code defines the final lifecycle notification and parses its result.
Tests show that session-end matcher reason selection is stable and successful hook output does not alter the outcome.
Session-start source and target types route the startup lifecycle event and determine its matcher input.
Stop request/target handling selects event-specific handlers and returns stop/continue outcomes, capturing terminal lifecycle behavior.
Prompt-submit request/outcome parsing includes a test that `continue=false` preserves context for later turns, clarifying mutation semantics.
The compatibility notifier preserves a historical notification wire shape and scrubs credentials before replaying session data.
The crate defines the event-name and matcher registries plus stable event-key helpers, the shared hook lifecycle vocabulary.
Typed `HookMcpCall`/`HookMcpOutput` and executor interfaces define the MCP-backed hook invocation boundary.
The output spiller stores large hook outputs under a dedicated directory and returns a bounded preview, controlling context growth.
Tests verify hook output stays inline when small, spills when large, and applies limits independently per context.
`HooksConfig`, `Hooks`, and plugin matching implement the runtime registry and configuration-replacement boundary.
This module binds checked-in generated event schema fixtures to named schema IDs, maintaining the machine-readable hook protocol.
Shared hook callback, result, response, and handler types define the lifecycle’s typed contract and abort behavior.
